newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street stocks higher at midday.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street stocks higher at midday.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were higher at midday due to strength in the bond market and the high technology sector, analysts said.
But the market was quiet and investors and money managers were wary of sticking their necks out ahead of Friday's October employment report and the U.S. election next Tuesday.

The Dow Industrials were up nine at 6003 while advances led declining issues by 11 to 10 on volume of about 225 million shares. U.S. Treasuries were firm, with the long bond up 8/32 to yield 6.69 percent.

"The market is assuming that the data tomorrow will not show reacceleration of the economy. That is being discounted by the market right now, so it had better be in line," said Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co.

"The amplitude of wage increases also better stay moderate or we are in trouble. With the Dow at 6000 and the long bond yield around 6.68, we are discounting a soft landing, no inflation pressures and an extended business cycle," he said.
Today's positive tone was set by strength in the high-tech sector, still a favorite of money managers looking for a place to invest.
The Nasdaq Composite Index, a barometer of the high techs, was up six at 1212 while Nasdaq advances held a lead over declines on volume of about 275 million shares.
High techs rallied after a forecast by the Semiconductor Industry Association that chip sales may be pulling out of their year-long slump and could grow 3.5 percent in the fourth quarter.
"That has helped sentiment in the group, especially coming at a time when the group was lagging," a trader said.
Intel Corp was up 1-3/4 at 108-1/2 and Cisco Systems Inc was up 1-3/8 at 59-1/2.

Metz said that the market was unlikely to rally following next Tuesday's U.S. election. Wall Street is discounting a victory by President Clinton over Republican challenger Bob Dole and on the Republicans holding both houses of Congress.

"That is what Wall Street wants and if it gets it, the market will sell off because it has been anticipated," he said. "If the Democrats carry Congress there will be some short-term concern about the temptation for a new spending binge. Markets will sell off."
He said in the unlikely event that Dole won, bonds would sell off in fear of his promised 15 percent tax cut.
Bonds responded positively to several pieces of economic data today.

September personal incomes rose a forecast 0.6 percent compared to a revised 0.5 percent increase in August while personal spending rose a lower than forecast 0.1 percent compared to a revised 0.5 percent the previous month.

The Chicago PMI rose to a higher than forecast 56.9 in October from a September reading of 56.3. But the increase was offset by a drop in the prices paid component, which fell to 50.7 from September's reading of 59.3.
Shares of Starbucks Corp were down two at 33 after the company reported weaker-than-expected same-store sales for October, the first month of its fiscal year.
Biogen Inc shares were down four at 74-1/4. The company said it was disappointed with a ruling by Britain's House of Lords dismissing a hepatitis B treatment patent.
